newsitem.title: GREECE: DEFENCE/DEVELOPMENT FALSE DILEMMA - DEFENCE MIN.
newsitem.headline: DEFENCE/DEVELOPMENT FALSE DILEMMA - DEFENCE MIN.

text.p: Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos said on Monday Greece must increase its arms spending to ensure its territorial integrity if it wants a stable economic environment within the European Union.

"The defence or development dilemma is a false one. Greece is under threat from Turkey and this must be faced despite the cost," he told a American-Hellenic Chamber of Commerce conference on the Greek economy.
"A proper defence is the pre-condition for stability and any development effort," he added.
He said Turkish threats against Greece had become more intense in the past year with specific territorial claims on Aegean islands.
"The status quo in the Aegean must be the foundation for Greek-Turkish relations. But Turkey wants to change this status quo. It wants to increase its vital space in the Aegean Sea," he said.
Turkey wanted to play a more important role in Europe and to join the EU "regardless of whether this happens in 10, 15 or 20 years," he said.

The Greek government decided this month to spend some four trillion drachmas on new arms in the next 10 years and Tsohatzopoulos said taxpayers will have to contribute about 120 billion drachmas on defense annually until the year 2000.
"The payment for the new arms is a long process. It will not upset our conergence programme with the EU," he said.
Greece will spend 4.2 percent of its GDP for defence needs this year. Prime Minister Costas Simitis has said Athens would also resort to foreign borrowing to come up with the necessary funds.
